label: blue-pottery-of-jaipur/chemistry/oxide-colours
title: Oxides and the colours they fire to
description: A table of the metal oxides painted on Jaipur blue pottery and the colour each gives after firing. Place it where the painting and firing of the ware are described.

u0001.text: Each metal oxide fires to its own colour on Jaipur ware.

u0002.text: Cobalt oxide fires to the deep blue that dominates the ware.

C003.text: The statement of case says the blue on the product is so dominant it is easily recognised, and cobalt-oxide blue is the key shade of its visual appeal.

quotes.quote: The blue colour on the product is so dominant that it can be easily recognised on the naked eye.
The brilliance of blue created from the cobalt oxide is striking and is the key shade to create the visual appeal of these items.

C021.text: On firing, the oxide of cobalt becomes deep blue, chromium turns green, cadmium gives bright yellow and iron oxide becomes red-brown.

quotes.quote: The oxide of cobalt becomes a deep blue, that of chromium changes to green, cadmium produces a bright yellow and iron oxide becomes a red-brown.
iron may be used for red, cadmium for yellow and chromium for green

C025.text: Ceramics Monthly lists the Jaipur colours as copper for turquoise, chromium for green, cobalt for dark blue and black, iron for brown, cadmium for yellow and manganese for purple.

quotes.quote: The colors of Jaipur pottery are as follows: copper to create turquoise; chromium to create green; cobalt to create dark blue and black; iron to create brown; cadmium to create yellow; and manganese to create purple.

S03.title: Statement of Case for Blue Pottery of Jaipur in Rajasthan
